I farm this land the way I have learned over many years: I keep the full 11.9 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that fits my land, my water, and the way I work. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on stable, moderate water instead of gambling on rainfall. I will not chase the highest-input approach. At my age, I want a plan that is steady, manageable, and dependable. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put most of the fertilizer in as a base, irrigate at the key stages, and keep weeds and disease under control with a limited number of sprays. After wheat harvest, I will move straight into summer maize on the same land. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me better stand and yield, keep fertilizer at a medium level, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and do only the pesticide work that is necessary. I will use simple tillage that saves labor and keeps the field in workable condition. My goal is not to do anything fancy. I will aim for a solid harvest from both crops with costs and labor kept under control.
